Requirement
Statement
Source
Rationale

REQ-DRIVING-036
reqEmergencyBrakingForImminentCollision
While the needed deceleration to a vehicle
ahead is at least 5.0 m/s², the driver-
assistance system shall command a
deceleration of at least 5.0 m/s².
NEED-DRIVING-008; SRC-UNECE-R152 emergency
braking; REQ-AEBS-003; gap
gapVehicleTargetCriteria; scenarios SC-
DRIVING-012 and SC-DRIVING-013
Derived from the emergency braking of the
car to car scenario of the source
regulation (SRC-UNECE-R152), which asks
for a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s²
once the system has detected the
possibility of an imminent collision, and
from REQ-AEBS-003. The requirement states
that condition in the world of the
vehicle, by the needed deceleration,
rather than as a detection by the system:
once avoiding a vehicle ahead needs 5.0
m/s², a smaller command no longer avoids
it. Up to a closing speed of 144 km/h a
needed deceleration of 5.0 m/s² comes with
a time to collision of at most 4.0 s, so
that the collision is then imminent and
REQ-DRIVING-041 lets the braking start;
the settings close at 60 km/h at most. The
obligation is the candidate's: the demand
is in its command. At 014e0e7a the
candidate writes the acceleration that its
speed planner returns to the vehicle in
each cycle that has an inference result
(longitudinal_planning.cpp:36;
vision_pilot.cpp:138, 157, 174), so it
already decelerates while it flags a
warning; its own emergency band starts
below -5.0 m/s² (planning.cpp:118). A
simulation cannot show the service brakes
and the anti-lock function of a real
vehicle, which turn the demand into a
deceleration.
test
Met when every setting of SC-DRIVING-012
and SC-DRIVING-013 is judged, and in each
judged run the last driving command of the
driver-assistance system holds a
deceleration of at least 5.0 m/s² at each
instant of the functional part at which
the needed deceleration to the target is
at least 5.0 m/s².
REQ-DRIVING-037
reqImpactSpeedWithinLimit
When a collision with a vehicle ahead is
imminent, the driver-assistance system
shall brake the vehicle to a relative
impact speed of at most the maximum
relative impact speed for the relative
approach speed.
NEED-DRIVING-008; SRC-UNECE-R152 speed
reduction by braking demand; REQ-AEBS-003;
gap gapVehicleTargetCriteria; scenarios
SC-DRIVING-012 and SC-DRIVING-013
This is a performance requirement on the
outcome of the braking. Derived from the
speed reduction by braking demand of the
car to car scenario of the source
regulation (SRC-UNECE-R152), with the test
speeds of its warning and activation tests
with a stationary and a moving vehicle
target, and from REQ-AEBS-003. The limits
and the test speeds are those of a car in
running order, because the simulated
vehicle carries no load. The relative
approach speed is taken when the collision
becomes imminent; at a constant approach
speed it is the speed of the setting less
that of the target, which gives a limit of
0 km/h in each setting except SC-
DRIVING-012 at 60 km/h, where it is 35
km/h. The source sets the limits for
unobstructed targets on a flat and dry
road, with the centre lines at most 0.2 m
apart, in daylight and on a straight road;
the settings and the judged runs keep
those conditions. The obligation is the
candidate's, with the simulated vehicle
and its brakes standing in for a real one
(asmSimulatedConfigurationStandsIn); the
settings are System 2's. A simulation
cannot show the target that the source
prescribes, a series production car or a
soft target, nor the measured road
surface, the illumination and the test
masses.
test
Met when every setting of SC-DRIVING-012
and SC-DRIVING-013 is judged, and the
relative impact speed of each judged run
is at most the maximum relative impact
speed for its relative approach speed.
REQ-DRIVING-038
reqDrivingCommandOverSCORE
The driver-assistance system shall give
its driving command to the actuation of
the vehicle only over the Eclipse S-CORE
path.
NEED-DRIVING-008; scope item
scoreCommandPathInScope; gap
gapScoreIntegration; scenarios SC-
DRIVING-012 to SC-DRIVING-015
This is a design constraint: the increment
judges the candidate on the S-CORE path of
the product line. A path around it, such
as a direct connection from the candidate
to the simulator, would let the vehicle
brake while S-CORE carries nothing. At
014e0e7a only the ROS 2 build of the
application reads a live speed and
commands a vehicle. That build connects to
topics (vision_pilot.cpp:59-64) and
publishes the steering and the
acceleration
(vehicle_ros2_interface.cpp:25-26); the
build without ROS 2 takes its vehicle
interface by the key source.mode
(vision_pilot.cpp:65-78): its CAN
interface reads a speed of zero and writes
nothing (can_interface.cpp:4-12), and its
file interface reads recorded speeds and
writes nothing (file_interface.cpp:37-61).
The application has no binding to S-CORE
(gapScoreIntegration). Phases 6 to 8
decide how the command enters the S-CORE
path. The no-autopilot, replay or overlay
condition of the planned reviews is a
criterion of this requirement.
test
Met when, in every run of SC-DRIVING-012
to SC-DRIVING-015, every driving command
that reaches the actuation is matched in
the communication records of the Eclipse
S-CORE path to a driving command of the
driver-assistance system; when the
autopilot and the traffic manager of the
simulator have no control of the vehicle
at any time of the run and no recorded,
replayed, scripted or overlaid control
reaches its actuation; and when, in one
further run of SC-DRIVING-012 in which the
Eclipse S-CORE path of the driver-
assistance system is stopped, no driving
command reaches the actuation after the
stop.
REQ-DRIVING-039
reqDetectableDrivingCommand
The driver-assistance system shall give
each driving command in a form that lets
the actuation detect its loss, delay,
repetition or corruption on the Eclipse
S-CORE path.
NEED-DRIVING-008; REQ-MW-006; gap
gapNoSeparateEmergencyFunction;
emergencyBrakingIndependenceConcern
This is a design constraint on the form of
the driving command. The product line
holds the independence of the protected
emergency command path as common content:
REQ-MW-006 obliges its products to prevent
a failure of the middleware integration
path from causing an uncontrolled
emergency intervention command, whatever
its realization. The candidate cannot keep
a path outside itself from failing. Its
share is a command whose loss, delay,
repetition or corruption the actuation can
detect; rejecting what the actuation
detects is the share of the product that
holds the path, under REQ-MW-006, and
phases 6 to 8 allocate both. At 014e0e7a
the candidate's braking leaves in its one
driving command (vision_pilot.cpp:157,
174), which REQ-DRIVING-038 sends over the
Eclipse S-CORE path
(gapNoSeparateEmergencyFunction). The
analysis rests on the realization that
phase 8 records and makes no freedom-from-
interference claim.
analyze
Met when the analysis of the realization
that phase 8 records shows, for a loss, a
delay, a repetition and a corruption of a
driving command on the Eclipse S-CORE
path, the part of the command by which the
actuation detects it.
REQ-DRIVING-040
reqWithholdWarningRequest
The driver-assistance system shall start
its warning request only while a collision
with a vehicle ahead is imminent.
NEED-DRIVING-009; SRC-UNECE-R152 false
reaction avoidance; REQ-AEBS-008; gap
gapVehicleTargetCriteria; scenarios SC-
DRIVING-012 to SC-DRIVING-015
Derived from the false reaction avoidance
of the source regulation (SRC-UNECE-R152),
which asks the system to minimise
collision warnings where no collision is
imminent and lists false-reaction
scenarios for an assessment, and from REQ-
AEBS-008. Phase 5 confirms the two
scenarios that phase 2 proposed from that
list, the curved road with guard pipes and
a stationary object (SC-DRIVING-014) and
the turn of a vehicle ahead (SC-
DRIVING-015). At the speeds and the times
to collision that the source names for
them no collision is imminent, so any
warning there is a false reaction. The
source gives those values as guidance, not
as a test: the settings take their
approach speeds, and System 2 records the
rest in each run. The requirement binds
the start of each warning request in every
run, in SC-DRIVING-012 and SC-DRIVING-013
too before the collision becomes imminent.
It binds the start rather than the whole
request, because braking can end the
imminence while the warning goes on, which
the source allows. The obligation is the
candidate's; the settings are System 2's.
A simulation cannot show the variety of
real roads that the assessment of the
source covers.
test
Met when, in every run of SC-DRIVING-012
to SC-DRIVING-015, a collision with a
vehicle ahead is imminent at the start of
each warning request of the driver-
assistance system.
REQ-DRIVING-041
reqWithholdEmergencyBraking
The driver-assistance system shall start
an emergency braking only while a
collision with a vehicle ahead is
imminent.
NEED-DRIVING-009; SRC-UNECE-R152 false
reaction avoidance; REQ-AEBS-012; gap
gapVehicleTargetCriteria; scenarios SC-
DRIVING-012 to SC-DRIVING-015
Derived from the false reaction avoidance
of the source regulation (SRC-UNECE-R152),
which asks the system to avoid emergency
braking where no collision is imminent,
and from REQ-AEBS-012. The candidate's
speed planner still slows the vehicle for
the curve and for the vehicle ahead
(longitudinal_planning.cpp:13-14, 34);
only a command for 5.0 m/s² or more is an
emergency braking. The requirement binds
the start of each emergency braking in
every run, in SC-DRIVING-012 and SC-
DRIVING-013 too before the collision
becomes imminent. It binds the start
rather than the whole braking, because a
braking harder than the needed
deceleration lowers it below 1.0 m/s²
before the vehicle stops, which ends the
imminence. The obligation is the
candidate's; the settings are System 2's.
A simulation cannot show the variety of
real roads that the assessment of the
source covers.
test
Met when, in every run of SC-DRIVING-012
to SC-DRIVING-015, a collision with a
vehicle ahead is imminent at the start of
each emergency braking of the driver-
assistance system.
REQ-DRIVING-042
reqWarningRequestBeforeEmergencyBraking
When a collision with a vehicle ahead is
imminent, the driver-assistance system
shall give a warning request at its
boundary at least 1.0 s of simulation time
before the start of its emergency braking.
NEED-DRIVING-010; SRC-UNECE-R152 collision
warning; REQ-AEBS-002; gap
gapWarningOutput; scenarios SC-DRIVING-012
and SC-DRIVING-013
Derived from the collision warning of the
car to car scenario of the source
regulation (SRC-UNECE-R152), which asks
for the warning to the driver at the
latest 0.8 s before the start of the
emergency braking, and from REQ-AEBS-002.
The source asks for the warning where the
relative speed is above the speed up to
which the vehicle can avoid the collision;
NEED-DRIVING-010 asks for the request
whenever a collision with a vehicle ahead
in its lane is imminent, and the
requirement follows the need. The
obligation is the candidate's for the
request and for its lead of 1.0 s. Of the
1.0 s, 0.2 s is allotted from the warning
request to the start of each mode of the
warning, on the display and as a sound.
That share is the obligation of the
Eclipse S-CORE path and the AAOS SDV,
which phases 6 to 8 allocate: each mode is
due within 0.2 s of wall-clock time after
the request, and so at least 0.8 s before
the start of the emergency braking while
the simulation runs no faster than wall-
clock time, which is the obligation of
System 2. The source lets the warning come
as late as the start of the emergency
braking when the collision cannot be
anticipated in time; in each setting at a
constant approach speed the collision
becomes imminent at least 1.11 s before a
needed deceleration of 5.0 m/s², so the
exception is not taken. At 014e0e7a the
application has no warning output at its
boundary, and its forward-collision
warning and its emergency braking are two
ranges of one planned acceleration
(planning.cpp:113-121; gapWarningOutput).
A simulation cannot show whether a driver
perceives the warning.
test
Met when every setting of SC-DRIVING-012
and SC-DRIVING-013 is judged, and in each
judged run in which the collision with the
target becomes imminent the driver-
assistance system gives a warning request
at its boundary, at least 1.0 s of
simulation time before the start of the
first emergency braking of the run when
the run has one.
REQ-DRIVING-043
reqWarningRequestOverSCORE
The driver-assistance system shall give
its warning request to the AAOS SDV only
over the Eclipse S-CORE path.
NEED-DRIVING-010; scope item
scoreCommandPathInScope; gaps
gapWarningOutput and gapScoreIntegration;
scenarios SC-DRIVING-012 and SC-
DRIVING-013
This is a design constraint: the warning
reaches the driver through the S-CORE path
of the product line to the AAOS SDV. At
014e0e7a the application's warnings go
only to its own visualization and data
log, each when it is switched on
(vision_pilot.cpp:177-185), and its
vehicle interface carries no warning
(gapWarningOutput). A data log can give
the evaluators a record of the warnings;
it is not a warning request. Phases 6 to 8
decide how the request leaves the
candidate.
test
Met when, in every run of SC-DRIVING-012
and SC-DRIVING-013, every warning request
that reaches the AAOS SDV is matched in
the communication records of the Eclipse
S-CORE path to a warning request of the
driver-assistance system, and when, in one
further run of SC-DRIVING-012 in which the
Eclipse S-CORE path of the driver-
assistance system is stopped, no warning
request reaches the AAOS SDV after the
stop.
REQ-DRIVING-044
reqRecordCandidateIdentity
The driver-assistance system shall record
its candidate identity before its first
driving command of each run.
NEED-DRIVING-011; gap
gapCandidateBehaviorUnverified; scenarios
SC-DRIVING-012 to SC-DRIVING-015
Another engineer can rerun a run only from
what it names, and a build with a change
that upstream has not merged is a
different candidate: the recorded
difference tells them apart. Source,
network files and configuration are pinned
separately, because none of them fixes the
others; the configuration is pinned by the
SHA-256 of each of its files and by the
settings of its launch, so that another
engineer can check each. The configuration
includes the run-time settings: at
014e0e7a, in a build without ROS 2, the
key source.mode chooses where the camera
image and the speed come from
(vision_pilot.cpp:65-78), and the key
speed_limit sets the highest speed that
the candidate's planner drives toward
(vision_pilot.conf:20). Like the run
identity of the closed-loop driving
increment (REQ-DRIVING-033), the record is
a behaviour of the candidate in each run,
which phase 6 allocates to a function. The
scenario and the simulated configuration
belong to System 2 and are pinned there.
test
Met when every run of SC-DRIVING-012 to
SC-DRIVING-015 has the record before its
first driving command; when another
engineer who checks out the named
revision, applies the recorded difference
and hashes the named network files and
configuration files obtains the recorded
values; and when a build with one change
that upstream has not merged records a
non-empty difference.
